editorial: This report contains trends that have emerged for the first time today, without repeating records included in normal reports from the last 30 days.

items.title: Homebrew/BrewUI
items.summary: Homebrew is a command-line tool used to manage software packages on the macOS operating system. BrewUI is the official desktop application that allows you to manage the complex commands of this tool with a graphical user interface (GUI).

items.title: danny-avila/LibreChat
items.summary: LibreChat is an open-source chat platform that combines different AI models and tools in a single interface. This software, which users can host on their own servers, offers a personalized AI experience with features such as model switching and multi-user authentication.

items.title: MG1937/ASC
items.summary: ASC is a very fast Android decompiler interface developed for mobile application researchers and AI agents. Written in Python, this tool aims to speed up the process of analyzing complex application files.

items.title: earendil-works/pi
items.summary: Pi is an AI agent toolkit that provides a unified interface for large language models and automates software development processes. It facilitates coding tasks by managing agent loops via a terminal-based user interface (TUI) and a command-line interface (CLI).

items.title: Show HN: An e-ink frame that hears birds and draws them as 1800s illustrations
items.summary: Fugleramme is a frame project that detects surrounding bird sounds with a microphone, converts them into 19th-century style illustrations, and displays them on an e-ink screen. The device combines real-time audio analysis with visual generation to offer a digital nature observation experience.

items.title: Introducing System One Models and Jev
items.summary: System One models, introduced by Typesafe, offer a new AI architecture designed to manage complex logical reasoning processes. These models work in conjunction with a runtime called Jev to make tasks such as debugging and system auditing more reliable in software development processes.

items.title: An update on Wayback Machine access
items.summary: The internet archiving service Internet Archive has shared updates regarding the Wayback Machine platform, which has been experiencing access issues due to cyberattacks and legal processes. The service aims to make access to past web pages stable again by strengthening its technical infrastructure.

items.title: Suspected sabotage causes major Netherlands rail disruption
items.summary: Large-scale disruptions in the Dutch railway network are believed to be caused by sabotage, according to investigations. This interference, which targeted the transportation system across the country, brings the issue of critical infrastructure security back to the agenda.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
items.summary: Google has announced new AI models, Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, focused on real-time interaction and in-depth reasoning. These models aim to produce more consistent and logical responses by using extended thinking capabilities to solve complex problems.

items.title: m-a-p/YuE2-3B
items.summary: YuE2-3B, shared on Hugging Face, is an artificial intelligence model that performs text-to-audio generation. It has the capability to process input text and convert it into high-quality audio files.

items.title: StepAudio 3 Realtime Technical Report
items.summary: StepAudio 3 Realtime is an audio-language foundation model that combines deep reasoning with low latency in voice interactions. Operating with a listen, speak, think, and act cycle, the system provides a natural dialogue flow thanks to its seamless duplex structure.

items.title: StepAudio 3 Music Technical Report
items.summary: StepAudio 3 Music is a large-scale model designed for long-form music generation, operating via text prompts. To maintain musical structure, the system processes audio data using a semantic-based tokenizer structure and utilizes a diffusion Transformer that works with a flow-matching method.

items.title: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration
items.summary: Decoy Direction Optimization is a defense method developed against refusal feature ablation attacks that disable safety constraints in open-weight large language models. This technique aims to protect safety layers by adjusting model weights without the need for high-cost fine-tuning processes.

items.title: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Emergence World is a multi-agent simulation environment designed to test the safety of autonomous systems working on long-term tasks. The system aims to identify errors that isolated tests cannot detect by monitoring the interaction of AI agents in processes such as memory and tool usage.

items.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: The concept of recursive self-improvement, which enables artificial intelligence systems to continuously improve their own capabilities and development processes, aims for systems to evolve without human intervention. This approach seeks to turn AI into a self-improving meta-process through autonomous strategy determination and experience acquisition stages.

items.title: A/I Shuts Down
items.summary: The Europe-based digital rights advocate and hosting service Autistici/Inventati has announced that it is ceasing operations due to interventions outside of legal processes. The closure of the platform, which hosted thousands of email accounts, blogs, and websites, has brought the debate on protecting independent digital infrastructure on the internet back to the agenda.

items.title: GEFS on OpenBSD: A very early preview
items.summary: GEFS, developed on the OpenBSD operating system, aims to provide a general framework for file systems. This structure allows different types of file systems to be integrated more easily at the kernel level.

items.title: Small Programming Tricks
items.summary: In software development processes, small and practical programming tricks rather than major architectural changes increase the sustainability of the system. These methods simplify complex structures, reduce the margin of error, and make the daily workflow of developers more efficient.
